pairs.why: B's booth is a bit larger and wider, filling about 85% of card height with a 3/4 angle like the real booth, while A's is narrower and sits smaller in the frame.
B's single tall building fills most of the card height and sits centered, like the real lighthouse. A's house is smaller and has two trees beside it that compete for attention.
B's chair is a little wider and larger in frame, and its 3/4 stance is nearer the real chair's footprint. A is narrower with more empty platform.
B's candelabra fills more of the card width and height, with a wide base and flames near the top edge, like the real hero objects. A is slimmer and leaves more empty space.
A and B have almost the same chair scale, placement and margins, so composition gives no reason to choose.
A's clock fills the card with a similar margin to the real one and sits on a plain striped wall. B adds a shelf and ground shadow that the real card doesn't have.
A's table is slightly larger and closer to the viewer, with less sky, so it reads a bit more like the real card's big, tightly framed hero. B pulls back more.
Both chairs have similar scale and margins. A is wider, B is taller, and neither is clearly nearer the real chair's framing.
